question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
answer:
The heaters ran for about eight hours. The tank is Oxygen tank No. 2, and before launch its heaters were run on 65-volt ground power to empty it: [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)".

The board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in that tank: [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)".

The board's report also points to the switches, calling their failure a serious oversight: [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)".

The tank's description says its switches failed under 65-volt power and caused the explosion: [[oxygen-tank-2]] description: "Apollo [unverified] 13 service module tank whose 28-volt thermostatic switches failed under 65-volt power and caused the explosion".

question: The astronaut who caught German measles before Apollo 13 set off a crew swap. What office did the astronaut brought in by that swap later win, and what happened?
answer:
The astronaut who caught German measles was Charlie Duke. He caught it from a friend's 3-year-old son about three weeks before the Apollo 13 launch [[charlie-duke]] "[stated] Caught German measles from a friend's 3-year-old son about three weeks before the Apollo 13 launch (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". His exposure set off the crew swap: Duke caught German measles and exposed the crews [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Backup lunar module pilot Charlie Duke caught German measles and exposed the crews (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". The swap replaced Ken Mattingly with Jack Swigert [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)".

Swigert later won a seat in the US House of Representatives. He was elected in 1982 but died before taking office [[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)".

question: The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was carried by a spacecraft. Which Apollo 11 crew member piloted that kind of spacecraft, and what did he do during the landing?
answer:
The tank was oxygen tank No. 2, which exploded on 1970-04-13 and crippled Apollo 13. The service module of the command and service module carried the oxygen tanks. Michael Collins was the command module pilot of Apollo 11, and during the landing he stayed in lunar orbit.

- The tank exploded during Apollo 13: [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- The service module carried the oxygen tanks: [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Its service module carried the oxygen tanks that supplied power and air (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"
- Collins was the command module pilot: [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Command module pilot of Apollo 11 (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)". The command module Columbia was part of the command and service module: [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Apollo 11's command module was Columbia (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- During the landing, Collins stayed in lunar orbit: [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- The landing itself was made by the lunar module Eagle, not by Collins: [[apollo-11]] "[stated] Lunar module Eagle landed on 1969-07-20 in the Sea of Tranquility (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The notes do not state directly that the oxygen tank was carried by the command and service module, only that the service module carried the oxygen tanks. The link from the tank note to the command and service module is a relation, not a fact line, so I have not cited it as a fact.

question: What was the improvised "mailbox" on Apollo 13 made from, and how did the crew build it?
answer:
The "mailbox" was an improvised adapter for Apollo 13's carbon dioxide scrubbers. The command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square, while the lunar module's were round ([[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)").

Engineers devised the adapter from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape ([[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] Engineers devised an adapter from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)").

The crew built it from radioed instructions ([[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The crew built it from radioed instructions (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)").

The notes don't give the step-by-step construction method or the adapter's dimensions.

question: How did the Cortright report describe the switch failure?

It recommended removing all electrical equipment from inside the oxygen tank pressure vessel: [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Recommended removing all electrical equipment from inside the oxygen tank pressure vessel (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)".

The board also traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2: [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)". It recommended redesigning the tank and removing electrical equipment from inside it: [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Recommended redesigning the oxygen tank and removing electrical equipment from inside it (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)".

The notes do not give the report's own technical wording on the switches. The switch details (28-volt switches under 65-volt heater power) come from a different source, Moonport SP-4204, so I have not attributed them to the Cortright report.

3. **1970-04-11: launch.** [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

4. **1970-04-13: oxygen tank explosion and abort.** Oxygen tank No. 2 exploded about 56 hours into the flight. The mission goal changed from a Fra Mauro landing to a safe return to Earth. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)". [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision) (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

5. **1970-04-17: splashdown.** The crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

6. **June 1970: review board report.** The Cortright board report was published. The brain gives only the month, not the day. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". The board traced the explosion to tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"
